endings.title: The Dry Summit
endings.epilogue: The pound fell below the sills and a grain barge settled on the stone like a tired animal. The canal closed for the season. The Company found the cause quickly: the Keeper. The reservoirs were not mentioned.

endings.title: The Breach
endings.epilogue: The east embankment went at the third bell. Halfway's low streets were under water by the fourth. They found the Keeper's ledger on the study table, dry, open at the day's figures.

endings.title: The Jam
endings.epilogue: Boats moored nose to tail from the summit to Lock 6. Aldmere embargoed the canal. The Company sent a telegram of eleven words, and a replacement.

endings.title: The Pile-Up
endings.epilogue: Two vessels met in the chamber at speed. The inquiry lasted three weeks and used the Keeper's name forty times. Nobody used the word 'throughput'.

endings.title: Foreclosure
endings.epilogue: The hands left when the wages stopped. The gates leaked. The Company seized the account and the post in the same letter, and Marguerite Cole bought the Keeper's furniture.

endings.title: The Audit
endings.epilogue: A surplus that large has only one explanation in the Company's manual. The auditor was courteous. The constables were not.

endings.title: Dismissal
endings.epilogue: The telegram arrived on a Tuesday. 'Appointment revoked. Vacate by the next watch.' Fennick read it twice before he handed it over, and did not sell a copy to anyone.

endings.title: The Promotion
endings.epilogue: They made the Keeper the face of the Meridian Canal Company in its eightieth year. When the water finally failed, the crowd knew exactly whose face to find.

endings.title: Run Out
endings.epilogue: The town did not shout. It barred its doors, cut the tow ropes, and walked the Keeper to the boundary stone in silence. Ilse Harrow carried the lamp.

endings.title: The Uprising
endings.epilogue: Halfway rose against the Company in the Keeper's name. The Company answered with a charge of sedition. The Keeper went east in irons, and the town went back to work.

endings.title: The Long Watch
endings.epilogue: A hundred watches. The Keeper retired to a cottage below Lock 7 and kept a garden that flooded every spring. The water went on falling, a mark at a time.

endings.title: Transferred
endings.epilogue: The Company moved the Keeper to a quiet lock on the Sorrel side. It was a promotion in every respect except the ones that mattered.

endings.title: The Jubilee Keeper
endings.epilogue: The Jubilee was magnificent, Pell said, and for once he was right. The Keeper's name is on the plaque beside the top gate. The plaque is bronze. Bronze does not rust, but it does go green.

endings.title: Town's Keeper
endings.epilogue: The town gave the Keeper a chair at the moot and a tankard with a name on it. The Company gave nothing. The Keeper stayed.

endings.title: Company's Keeper
endings.epilogue: Reliable, the file said. Reliable is the Company's highest word. The Keeper kept the gate for years and never once opened the sluice house.

endings.title: A Quiet Life
endings.epilogue: There was a wedding at the Still Water chapel and the geese were invited. The water fell a mark a watch, and someone else would have to notice.

endings.title: The Drought Report
endings.epilogue: The survey was published. The Company thanked the engineer, blamed the weather, raised tolls, and commissioned a tenth reservoir that would take twelve years to fill. The water fell a mark a watch.

endings.title: Dray's Killer
endings.epilogue: Vosk was removed on suspicion of murder. She went without a word. A new auditor arrived the next week, younger, and asked the Keeper the same questions in the same order.

endings.title: The Sorrel Purchase
endings.epilogue: Vane's consortium bought the Sorrel half of the canal. Tolls fell. Traffic rose. The Keeper was retained at a better wage. In the second summer the pound fell to the sills and nobody in Sorrel knew why.

endings.title: The Clearance
endings.epilogue: The Reed Reach was cleared without a shot. The boats went down the west flight and did not come back. Halfway was quieter. Nobody sang at the summit again, and the water fell a mark a watch.

endings.title: The Dry Blessing
endings.epilogue: The Lamp Vigil lasted nine nights and on the tenth it rained for a week. The pound rose. The chapel filled. The Keeper knelt with the rest and did not ask the water where it came from.

endings.title: Keeper of the Courier
endings.epilogue: Hesse made the Keeper famous on both shores. The Company could not dismiss a hero. It gave the Keeper a lecture tour instead, and the summit a new Keeper, and the sluice house a new lock.

endings.title: Into the Dark Water
endings.epilogue: The tunnel behind the sluice house went down and then it went under. The lamp lasted long enough to show a second lamp, rusted, and a coat that had been Dray's. The Ledger records what the Keeper saw, if not the Keeper.

endings.title: The Figures Do Not Close
endings.epilogue: The Keeper was dismissed within a watch of reading the survey. Quenn copied it out by hand before the drawer was emptied, and put the copy in the Ledger.

endings.title: The Last Verse
endings.epilogue: At the boundary stone Petronel sang the last verse, the one about the river that went into the hill. The town heard it too. The Ledger has the words.

endings.title: What the Water Uncovered
endings.epilogue: The Breach emptied the undercroft into the street. Among the wreckage were letters in an engineer's hand, and Hale, gathering them, gave one to the Ledger.

endings.title: Filed
endings.epilogue: The auditors found the Keeper with Vosk's Y31 file open on the desk. The Keeper was removed. The file was not, because Fennick had already wired its first page to the Ledger.

endings.title: The Gauge Speaks
endings.epilogue: On the last night the cipher gave way. The ledger was a map. Mirren read it over the Keeper's shoulder and said nothing, and kept it.

endings.title: Duly Noted
endings.epilogue: Crane filed his report under Schedule Nine. It included six years of water counts. Aldmere did not read it. The Ledger did.

endings.title: Tobin's Last Story
endings.epilogue: Old Tobin died in the spring and left the Keeper a tankard and a story about men who came at night to dredge a reservoir with no dredgers. The Keeper wrote it down.

endings.title: The Outfall
endings.epilogue: At the boundary stone Bram Holloway stood, which he did not do, and named a place on the north bank where the water comes out of the hill. The Ledger has the bearing.

endings.title: For the Record
endings.epilogue: Vosk delivered the dismissal herself. Then, for the record, she told the Keeper what the Company had known since the Dry Year, and left the door open behind her.

endings.title: The Boatyard Fire
endings.epilogue: Tamm's yard burned to the waterline with the season's hulls in it. The town blamed the Company. The Company blamed the Keeper. The Keeper had been holding a bucket.

endings.title: The Riot
endings.epilogue: It started at the inn and ended at the top gate. Nobody remembers who threw the first lamp. The Company's report said 'the Keeper failed to prevent'. Ilse's said nothing at all.

endings.title: The Frost Closure
endings.epilogue: The west flight froze with forty boats in the pound and the Company store half empty. When the ice went, so did the Keeper, quietly, on the first barge down.

endings.title: The Inquiry
endings.epilogue: Commissioner Kell chaired. The finding took four minutes. The Keeper's signature was on the order, and orders are what the Company keeps.

endings.title: The Fever
endings.epilogue: The fever came up the east flight in a boat with a clean bill. Stroud sat with the Keeper at the end and said, honestly, that there had been nothing to be done. She was not certain it was true.

endings.title: The River Returned
endings.epilogue: They opened Marrow's sluice at dawn and the Quell went home. The pound fell to a seasonal road. The Hullfolk went down the west flight to a valley their grandparents had left, and the Reed Reach remembers a Keeper who was a gate.

endings.title: The Open Ledger
endings.epilogue: Under the Compact, with Crane's seal and Quenn's figures and Hesse's front page, the truth was filed on both shores in the same watch. The Company lost the charter. A real reservoir took nine years. The canal lived.

endings.title: The Keeper's Cut
endings.epilogue: With Vosk's file, Hale's letters and Tamm's hands, the regulating sluice Marrow died building was finished. The pound holds. Lowmere has a stream again. Nobody knows, and the Ledger records that the Keeper chose to be the next Vosk.
